headline: Videos of two unrelated video games mashed together by AI-written mods are flooding social media, and many veteran modders are not pleased.
score_reason: Pool score kept; amusing trend with a real debate about AI and creative work, but mostly short clips.
importance_line: Game modders and players are affected first, then game studios whose code is being copied; the clips often hide broken gameplay, and the legal status of using decompiled code is unsettled.
summary: GLITCHED reports that clips of games combined with AI-assisted mods, such as Minecraft inside Elden Ring or Spider-Man swinging through Batman: Arkham Knight, have spread across social media in the past week, with the work largely attributed to the Claude Opus 5.5 coding model. It adds that in many cases the two games simply run side by side, early examples are glitchy, and some modders, including ones who use AI themselves, say the trend floods their scene with low-effort experiments.
notes: Trend began before 6 Oct (posts from late September); the summary says it ran over the past week.
